headline: Colombia: cannabis flower exports hit 13.8 tonnes, passing 2025
dek: Colombia shipped 13.8 tonnes of dried cannabis flower in January-September 2026, Cannamonitor found, already more than all of 2025, mostly to Europe.
key_points: Colombia exported 13.8 tonnes of dried cannabis flower in the first nine months of 2026, above the 13.0 tonnes of all 2025 and the 5.6 tonnes of 2024, according to Cannamonitor's analysis of customs declarations published on 25 November.
Prices split three ways: about US$882 a kg for pharmaceutical flower, US$530 for high-THC flower sent to EU processing hubs and about US$240 for CBD-rich flower to Switzerland and Czechia.
Germany and Poland take most high-THC flower; Poland's imports jumped from 0.3 tonnes in 2025 to 1.6 tonnes in nine months.
One exporter, Clever Leaves, shipped 51% of export value, and only three Colombian sites hold an EU-GMP certificate, the analysis found.
body: Colombia's medical cannabis industry, long better known for licences than for sales, is finally shipping meaningful volumes of flower. The country exported 13.8 tonnes of dried cannabis flower between January and September 2026, already more than the 13.0 tonnes it shipped in the whole of 2025 and well over double the 5.6 tonnes of 2024. The figures come from an analysis published on 25 November by Cannamonitor, a Barcelona-based cannabis market intelligence firm, using export declarations filed with Colombia's tax and customs authority, DIAN.

The growth is real but narrow. Cannamonitor found that the trade runs through three distinct corridors with very different buyers and prices, and that one company accounts for about half of all export value. For European importers and EU-GMP processors, the data are a map of where Colombian product actually goes and at what price.

Total cannabis exports, counting flower, extracts, isolate, finished medicines, biomass, seeds and cuttings, were worth US$16.6 million in 2025 and US$13.4 million in January-September 2026, the analysis said. Cannamonitor noted that the 2026 figure covers only nine months, so a lower value is not by itself a decline.

Colombia has more than 900 licensed cultivators, but the number of companies actually exporting fell from 38 in 2025 to 31 in 2026. Clever Leaves shipped 51% of export value across 2025 and the first nine months of 2026, about twice as much as the next five exporters combined. PharmaCielo, mainly in CBD isolate and extracts, was second.

The first corridor is pharmaceutical flower for regulated medical markets: all flower to Germany, Poland, Australia, Israel and Chile. It averaged about US$882 a kilogram free on board in 2026. Psychoactive flower makes up 75% of Colombian flower sent to Germany, and Poland's intake of psychoactive flower rose from 0.3 tonnes in all of 2025 to 1.6 tonnes in nine months of 2026. The largest single buyer across the period was Canify, which runs an EU-GMP site in Bavaria, followed in flower by Suprobion in Poland and Demecan in Saxony.

The second is high-THC flower sent to EU conversion hubs in Portugal, Malta, Czechia, Spain, the Netherlands and North Macedonia, where it is processed further. That flower averaged about US$530 a kilogram in 2026.

The third is CBD-rich commodity flower, which Colombia classes as non-psychoactive because it contains less than 1% THC. Switzerland and Czechia take 81% of it: 7.2 tonnes so far in 2026, at about US$240 a kilogram. Czechia alone rose from 1.2 tonnes to 3.5 tonnes. Pharmaceutical flower therefore sells for roughly 3.7 times the price of CBD flower.

Brazil is the odd one out. It bought no flower at all, yet it was Colombia's largest market by value, taking US$9.3 million or 31% of exports across the 21 months in medicines, CBD isolate and extracts. Finished products to Brazil fell while isolate rose, which Cannamonitor linked to Brazil's shift toward approved pharmacy products.
> Colombia does not have one cannabis export business. It has three, and only one of them earns pharmaceutical prices.

Not every market is growing. Flower exports to Australia fell from 2.2 tonnes in 2025 to 0.2 tonnes in the first nine months of 2026, while Thailand shipped 26.9 tonnes to Australia, the analysis said. Thai customs recorded 103 tonnes under the flower code in January-September 2026, including growing low-cost shipments to Switzerland and Czechia, the same CBD channel Colombia relies on.

Quality certification is the other constraint. Only three Colombian sites hold an EU-GMP certificate listed in the EU's EudraGMDP database, according to Cannamonitor: BG Labs, Clever Leaves and Pideka, whose 2023 certificate awaits renewal. Six more are certified to GACP standards and supply EU-GMP converters. Cannamonitor argued that price alone does not explain Colombia's loss of the Australian market.

Europe's medical markets are where Colombia's premium volume goes, and they are price-sensitive. As we reported on 18 November, Germany imported about 201 tonnes of medical cannabis in 2025, and, as we reported on 25 November, its federal drug commissioner has said imports are expected to exceed 300 tonnes this year. Against that, Colombia's psychoactive shipments are small, but the corridor is growing, and Poland's sharp rise suggests buyers there are diversifying supply.

Colombia allows licensed cultivation, processing and export for medical and scientific use, while adult-use commerce remains illegal, according to MetaFlora's Colombia legal hub. That leaves the industry entirely dependent on foreign regulated buyers and on the certification those buyers demand.

Watch whether Pideka's EU-GMP certificate is renewed and whether more Colombian sites win EU-GMP status, which would widen access to the higher-priced pharmaceutical corridor. Watch Thai competition in the CBD flower trade to Switzerland and Czechia, and whether Poland's demand keeps rising. Full-year DIAN data for 2026 will show whether Colombia's flower exports clear the 13.8 tonnes already shipped by a wide margin.
